guide.summary: OpenProject documents OAuth2 authorization code flow with user-bound bearer tokens. The api_v3 scope is the documented scope for the standard API and is the least-privilege documented option for reading work packages. Work package list endpoint GET /api/v3/work_packages supports offset and pageSize pagination, and the collection docs describe offset and cursor pagination. Each customer instance needs an admin-created OAuth application with a redirect URI and client credentials. Access is limited to what the connected person can see; the MissingPermission error confirms this.

findings.title: Authorization code flow issues user-bound bearer tokens for API calls
findings.detail: OpenProject documents an authorization code flow that yields an access token and refresh token. Requests with the bearer token act on behalf of the current user, so the connected person's own visibility applies.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer connects their own account on their own instance using developer-owned OAuth.

evidence.quote: Authorization code flow example
With the token that you obtained above you can now make API calls to the OpenProject instance on behalf of the current user.
The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.

findings.title: api_v3 scope grants access to the standard OpenProject API
findings.detail: Scopes are selected when the OAuth application is created. api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope. If no scope is checked, api_v3 is assumed. The scope is broad across the standard API; the actual boundary is the connected user's permissions, and this request only calls read endpoints.
findings.appliesWhen: Read-only work package title retrieval through the standard API.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the

steps.title: User consent redirect and callback check
steps.detail: Send the connected user to the documented authorization URL on their instance. The user approves access in the browser. OpenProject redirects to the redirect URI with a code parameter. Confirm the callback receives code and matches the expected state. This is an unexecuted step for the developer to perform with a real user account.
steps.doneWhen: The browser lands on the redirect URI with a code parameter and no error parameter.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
Typically the server that was requested with that redirect will save the authorization code and use it to obtain API token, with which the server can then act on behalf
In this example we skip that server side implementation and just copy the value of the code parameter from the URL that you see in your browser.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
REDIRECT_URI: URL-encoded callback configured in the application

steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in and refresh_token and scope api_v3.

steps.title: Read first page of accessible work package titles
steps.detail: GET <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>/api/v3/work_packages with Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN> and Accept: application/hal+json, using offset and pageSize (e.g. offset=1&pageSize=25). Read-only: send no write or delete requests. Read each subject from _embedded.elements. Results are limited to work packages the user can see. Pagination is required; use total and count to track progress. While a nextByOffset link is returned, request it and collect subjects from each page. Stop only when no nextByOffset link is returned. Two pages is not a complete listing. Boundary check: request a work package the user cannot see and expect MissingPermission, or confirm only permitted items appear. If no denial is documented, inspect granted scope and the request log.
steps.doneWhen: All pages were followed via nextByOffset until no further nextByOffset link was returned; every element's subject was collected and the count matches total; the boundary check is recorded as MissingPermission or as only permitted items shown; the request log contains no write or delete calls.
